title: Radical Equations
summary: Solve an equation with a variable under a radical by isolating the radical and raising both sides to the matching power. Squaring can introduce extraneous solutions, so every candidate must be checked in the original equation.

radical equation.plain: An equation with the variable under a root.
radical equation.in_class: Isolate the radical, then power both sides.

isolate the radical.plain: Get the root alone before powering up.

square both sides.plain: Raise to the power that cancels the root.
square both sides.in_class: Squaring for square roots, cubing for cube roots.

extraneous root.plain: A candidate that fails the original.
extraneous root.in_class: Introduced by squaring; must be discarded.

index.in_class: Raise both sides to this power to clear it.

check required.plain: Always verify in the original equation.

two radicals.plain: Equations with more than one root.
two radicals.in_class: Isolate one, square, isolate the other, square again.

domain restriction.plain: Radicands of even roots must be $\ge0$.

concept_sections.heading: Isolate then power
concept_sections.explanation: Get the radical by itself, then raise both sides to the index's power to remove it. For a square root, square both sides.
math_steps: Move everything else to the other side.
Raise both sides to the index power.

concept_sections.heading: Checking for extraneous roots
concept_sections.explanation: Squaring can create solutions that don't satisfy the original. Substitute each candidate back and keep only those that work.

concept_sections.heading: Two radicals
concept_sections.explanation: When two radicals appear, isolate one and square, then isolate the remaining radical and square again to eliminate both.

concept_sections.heading: Higher-index roots
concept_sections.explanation: For a cube root, cube both sides; for an $n$-th root, raise to the $n$-th power. Odd roots don't create extraneous solutions the way even roots can, but checking is still wise.
math_steps: Match the power to the index.

concept_sections.heading: Domain awareness
concept_sections.explanation: Even roots require nonnegative radicands, and a square root outputs a nonnegative value — so an equation like $\sqrt{x}=-2$ has no solution.
math_steps: A principal root can't equal a negative.

real_world_examples.title: Pendulum period
real_world_examples.scenario: Period depends on the square root of length.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: Solving $T=2\pi\sqrt{L/g}$ for $L$ squares both sides — a radical equation.

real_world_examples.title: Skid-mark speed estimate
real_world_examples.scenario: Police estimate speed from skid length.
real_world_examples.how_the_math_applies: The speed formula involves a square root; solving for length squares it.
